operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case table names (Addresses, Customer_Addresses, Order_Items) and mixed-case columns; must double-quote with original spelling.
DDL uses backtick quoting; sqlite_master DDL must be replayed verbatim into the empty clone.

DATETIME columns store TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' (space separator, no T, no fractional seconds); declared type contains 'date' -> Date fuzzer, but ts_fuzzer note says 'Date|Number(int elements)' because first element is not int.
All DATETIME columns are text storage, contradicting nothing but the Date template must be %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S to match samples.
Customer_Addresses, Customer_Contact_Channels, Order_Items have NO primary key (pk=[]); composite-key logic must handle empty PK (no PK-duplicate drop).
FKs all resolve to existing parents (parent_exists true); no dangling FKs, no self-references, no non-unique parents (all parents are INTEGER PRIMARY KEY).

Tiny tables: Addresses 15, Products 3, Customers 15, Customer_Addresses 15, Customer_Contact_Channels 20, Customer_Orders 15, Order_Items 15 rows; choose_table_sizes will massively oversize vs original.
order_quantity is VARCHAR(15) but stores integer-looking strings ('5','9','2'); String fuzzer will add str(i+1)/str(i-1) neighbours.
zip_postcode VARCHAR(20) stores short numeric strings ('416','721'); String fuzzer, not Number.
country has distinct=1 ('USA'); state_province_county distinct=12 with no spaces ('SouthCarolina'); other_address_details and other_customer_details are mostly/all NULL (null_rate 1.0 / 0.867).
contact_number VARCHAR(50) stores phone-like strings with dots/dashes/parens/x; String fuzzer charset a-zA-Z 0-9() will not reproduce punctuation.
payment_method, address_type, channel_code, order_status are small enums (2-5 distinct) stored as VARCHAR; String fuzzer will generate random strings, not enum members.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on all *_id INTEGER PKs: uniform in [-10^0,10^0] with int perturbation +-1/+-2; will produce ids far outside 1..15/1..3 and negatives.

Date fuzzer on all DATETIME columns: template %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S, range from min/max of 5 sampled originals (e.g. 2018-02..2018-03 for Customers), so fresh dates cluster in a narrow 2018 window; other tables (Customer_Addresses 1972..2010) get wide ranges.

String fuzzer on VARCHAR columns: random strings over a-zA-Z 0-9() of length up to declared length, plus 50% contaminate; will not match enum values (Cash/Cheque/Credit Card, Billing/Residential, Email/Cell/...), phone formats, or 'USA'.

FK columns (customer_id, address_id, order_id, product_id) draw from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement -> duplicates and ties in child tables; parent PKs are unique so FK values are valid but heavily repeated.
No PK on Customer_Addresses/Customer_Contact_Channels/Order_Items -> no PK-duplicate drop; rows can be fully duplicated, driving FP on DISTINCT/COUNT queries.
Tiny original tables (3-20 rows) vs choose_table_sizes (30..2500) -> generated instances are 10-100x larger; queries with COUNT/aggregate thresholds will behave very differently.

NOT NULL columns (payment_method, date_address_from, address_type, channel_code, active_from_date, contact_number, order_status, all FK cols) are not enforced in Python; String/Date fuzzers can emit NULL only via element dropout, so most inserts succeed but some rows fail at insert and are skipped.
order_quantity VARCHAR storing ints: String fuzzer adds str(i+1)/str(i-1) so numeric-looking values survive; comparisons like order_quantity > '5' may flip.

other_address_details / other_customer_details / order_details mostly NULL: String sampler with 5 originals (mostly None) drops None -> may have few elements, p may be 1 -> mostly fresh random strings, losing the NULL-heavy distribution.
Date fuzzer p-inversion: p=0.2 means element returned w.p. 0.2, fresh date w.p. 0.8 -> most dates are fresh uniform in the narrow original range, few exact originals; ties on date equality rare.

Enum columns (payment_method, address_type, channel_code, order_status) with 2-5 distinct: String fuzzer generates random strings, so WHERE payment_method='Cash' returns 0 rows in generated instances -> FN on enum-filter queries.
